nodes.label: Connector confirmations and large mutation plans
Explicit Thing presentation
nodes.rationale: Renderer choice is explicit crystal metadata; a saved pointer does not grant access to its Component or dependencies.

nodes.label: Environment API gateway ingress
nodes.rationale: Dedicated mode executes its own backend and refuses relay traffic; it does not imply an isolated database.

nodes.label: Device identity, disconnect, and Character discovery
nodes.rationale: Edge refusal must remain distinct from missing capabilities, authentication, and membership.

nodes.label: Paired Mac inventory and approved Bash
nodes.rationale: Script leases require explicit approved envelopes.

nodes.label: Timeline named versions, undo, and export
Action outcomes and recovery
nodes.rationale: Safe effect receipts are retained in the existing Timeline rather than a new history store or growing array.

nodes.label: Timeline related history
nodes.rationale: Shared definitions never expose another author's private event graph.

nodes.label: Scoped home Timeline storage
nodes.rationale: ownerId and dataPlane remain authorization and identity fences; scoped home context applies without changing the surrounding request's database selection.

nodes.label: Root data-plane precondition
nodes.rationale: The precondition checks selected source before explicit routing and grants no access.

nodes.label: Saved theme history
nodes.rationale: Approved token versions and retained deletion are recorded in the content transaction; no new endpoint or collection is introduced.

nodes.label: API access and route registry
nodes.rationale: All data access goes through /api/v1/...; Nitro routes documented endpoints to one catch-all handler, while the docs registry is the source of truth for route tables and both capability manifests.

nodes.label: Adding or changing an endpoint
nodes.rationale: Endpoint work follows an ordered procedure covering route registration, import map, docs registry, rate limiting, client negotiation, tests, and documentation.

nodes.label: Lopu continuity and native activity contracts
nodes.rationale: Uncertain work never replays; continuation claims persist until output is saved and completion is acknowledged.

nodes.label: API Endpoints and Capabilities Feature Map
Unified Timeline
nodes.rationale: Timeline uses immutable operations, revision fencing, refusal on divergence, and a canonical registered route to preserve published content and shared version and branch behavior.

nodes.label: Lopu Action Inspection
nodes.rationale: Read-only action inspection reuses execution resolution and input validation, while tests cover confirmation ordering, revoked reads, and incomplete contracts.

nodes.label: Lopu Thing Inspection
nodes.rationale: Bounded, lossless inspection walks only authorized public crystal data and uses pointers, revisions, and offsets to select pages without relaxing ACLs.

nodes.label: Lopu Page Contexts
nodes.rationale: Dirty and ready flags and omitted blocks are preserved across transport; missing blocks are not treated as an empty page.

nodes.label: Capability Verification Checks
nodes.rationale: Verification checks registered routes against the capability manifest, smoke-tests the built discovery response, and checks endpoint documentation responses.

nodes.label: MongoDB Health Failure Shape
nodes.rationale: Remote health probes preserve a complete sanitized status shape and avoid forwarding the local session cookie; HTTP 200 does not imply connectivity.

nodes.label: API Gotchas
nodes.rationale: Auth modes, private no-store responses for private data, and duplicate-key detection address authorization, caching, and configuration hazards.

nodes.label: Remote Filesystem Commands
nodes.rationale: Filesystem access is constrained to bounded device commands with closed shapes, leases, fences, exact ownership checks, short-lived bytes, and client capability negotiation.

nodes.label: Integration Library Runtime
nodes.rationale: Provider operations are fixed and read-only, upstream transport is bounded and redacted, browser SDKs are separately restricted, and browser keys stay out of saved Things.

nodes.label: Browser Action Programs
nodes.rationale: Browser behavior is represented as saved program data and interpreted through shared runtime contracts rather than endpoint-specific UI behavior.

nodes.label: Live Web Platform Form Event Programs
nodes.rationale: Generic native method and event backing supports form events while CSP confines explicit permission and prevents form navigation.

nodes.label: JavaScript Intrinsic and Constructor Programs
nodes.rationale: New language behaviors are composed from existing language nodes and the data compiler, avoiding additional execution endpoints and runtime permissions.

nodes.label: Reusable Binding and Assignment Patterns
nodes.rationale: Bounded pattern nodes extend the existing catalogue and Component runtime without introducing an execution endpoint or permission.

nodes.label: Web IDL Option and Callback Programs
nodes.rationale: Existing catalogue Actions emit complete editable programs for native APIs, so no new endpoint, runtime grant, or storage shape is needed.

nodes.label: Native Live Event Bindings
nodes.rationale: Saved event bindings are shared data used by renderer, compiler, and existing Thing persistence, avoiding endpoint or permission expansion.

nodes.label: Native Media Component Programs
nodes.rationale: Reusable media policy, live media, and DOM binding interpretation back editable examples; save and reopen preserve opaque program data and the private write boundary.

nodes.label: Canvas Catalogue Programs
nodes.rationale: Bounded surface roots, native receiver and resource limits, and editable program data permit canvas work without exposing the runtime Document or unrelated tree mutation.

nodes.label: SVG Catalogue Programs
nodes.rationale: Namespace-aware programs use bounded receivers and local resources; primitive IDL constants avoid constructor handles while storage, endpoints, and CSP remain unchanged.

nodes.label: CSS Typed OM Programs
nodes.rationale: Registered native CSS operations use the existing opaque receiver bridge, catalogue, and save contracts.

nodes.label: CSSOM Programs
nodes.rationale: Generic CSSOM contracts bound stylesheet and rule access and fence late native promise replies while retaining canonical catalogue and save contracts.

nodes.label: Observer Programs
nodes.rationale: Observer targets, options, receivers, callbacks, completion, and stop behavior are bounded and run-owned within the existing worker transport.

nodes.label: Range Programs
nodes.rationale: Owned native ranges and bounded contextual fragments extend the existing DOM bridge.

nodes.label: Animation Programs
nodes.rationale: Native objects, keyframes, and options are bounded; the existing bridge transports promises and callbacks and cancels animations on completion or stop.

nodes.label: ARIA Object Programs
nodes.rationale: Bounded nullable Element reflection and owned relationships preserve native frozen-list and element identity through the existing worker bridge.

nodes.label: Lopu Action Access
nodes.rationale: Per-chat Ask/Full mode gates mutations and Action execution; a shared import map supports delegable routes and is included in Nitro route registration.

nodes.label: Timeline Named-Branch Comparison
nodes.rationale: Branch comparison reuses the exact fenced head, shared merge base, canonical draft merge event, and ordinary branch advancement without adding endpoint, schema, or collection.

nodes.label: Timeline Branch Checkout
nodes.rationale: Checkout materializes an exact branch revision and head as a transient snapshot while ordinary client events and branch commands remain the only branch-edit writes.

nodes.label: Private Component Previews
nodes.rationale: Component previews reuse a bounded viewer-only resolver scoped to exact account and source, without granting page or root access.

nodes.label: Timeline Component Reads
nodes.rationale: Exact event and source scope, dependency and response-size limits, and stale-source refusals keep component reads bounded and private.

nodes.label: Timeline Component Merge Choices
nodes.rationale: Optional merge choices return bounded component-link maps and captures, with metadata preflight and aggregate response limits; no new route, collection, or schema is introduced.

nodes.label: Password Manager
nodes.rationale: Secret handling is isolated to controlled drafts and protected vault flows; private API mutations are revision-fenced, projections are secret-free, and clients avoid shared diagnostics and caches.

nodes.label: API Endpoints and Capabilities Feature Map
Password Migration Coverage and Encrypted File Lifecycle
General Compressor Storage
nodes.rationale: Supports validated intrinsic media containers with separately editable children without introducing an image-byte HTTP endpoint.

nodes.label: Mapbox Provider Integration
nodes.rationale: Provider destinations are fixed and responses are redacted; the application permits only required Mapbox service and events origins without allowing remote scripts or eval.

nodes.label: Storage Readiness and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Recovery uses transactional queue, worker and controller gates with an existing protected scheduler; failure response bodies are not logged.

nodes.label: Connections Catalog and OAuth
nodes.rationale: Owner-private encrypted grants replace shared tokens, with OAuth app configuration scoped to exact origin and environment.

nodes.label: Environment Gateway and Index Readiness
nodes.rationale: Durable index readiness is coordinated without blocking read-only authentication.

nodes.label: Public Social Metadata
nodes.rationale: Anonymous metadata uses an explicit allowlist and generic output for private or missing content; caller identity and remote URLs are not resolved.

nodes.label: Named Connections Management
nodes.rationale: The named endpoint verifies the exact actor, origin, connection ID and fixed operation, and token envelopes never cross the response boundary.

nodes.label: Connection Provider Artwork
nodes.rationale: The public asset stays on the document origin without opening a data-plane connection or forwarding user headers to the provider.

nodes.label: Dynamic Map Workspaces
nodes.rationale: Editable upload blocks, authorized overlays and canonical ACL-checked list pages support dynamic map workspaces.

nodes.label: Things Exact Counts and Visible List Windows
nodes.rationale: Count and list reuse the same canonical scope and exact ACL gates.

nodes.label: Maps Autocomplete and Query Batches
nodes.rationale: Inputs are validated before key access, duplicates share provider calls, and failures never return partial results.

nodes.label: Things Ordered Exact Reads
nodes.rationale: Missing, denied and protected positions are null; canonical ACLs and projections are shared with single reads.

nodes.label: Action URL Component Encoding
nodes.rationale: The encoding expression handles URL components without performing HTTP operations and refuses unsupported types or malformed UTF-16.

nodes.label: Large Editable Webpage Capture
nodes.rationale: Iterative Timeline traversal removes hidden block-count and depth write limits while retaining existing authorization and capture contracts.

nodes.label: Bounded Mac Byte Transport
nodes.rationale: Native transport negotiates independently and reuses canonical attachment routes; publication remains the existing guarded Files contract.

nodes.label: Shared-Content Request Transport
nodes.rationale: The scoped JSON reader authorizes and applies rate limits before streaming fatal UTF-8 decoding; completion enumerates parts server-side and presigning pages them.

nodes.label: Reviewed Creation Projections and Execution Admission
nodes.rationale: Creation progress is owner-only, and execution holds prevent server, browser, shared and child admission until review.
